data.narrative:
Exodys Energy is a Seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Carl Perez and Jean-Christophe Piroux that has raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Nano Nuclear Energy, X-Energy, Fuse Energy, and Applied Atomics.

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable valuation approach. Using total capital raised ($10M) as a proxy for seed-stage value, the analysis applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression, yielding an implied valuation of $25M. The Peer-Median method was not applied due to insufficient narrow peer datapoints; while 4 same-sector peers exist, the filtered set (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier) contains fewer than three comparable transactions, making sector-median extrapolation unreliable.

The triangulated valuation range is $21M to $29M, with a median of $25M. This reflects a single-method analysis anchored to capital deployed and stage-typical progression metrics. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct comparable transaction data within Exodys' specific stage and tier, reliance on a single methodology, and the inherent volatility in early-stage nuclear technology valuations. A more robust triangulation would require either sufficient peer transaction data or forward-looking metrics (IP depth, regulatory milestones, burn rate) to narrow the range.
